title: Design System: Samuel Chen — Working Papers

ink-faint.note: Chosen to clear 4.5:1 against --stock-band at 12-13px, not against the raised sheet.

manila.note: Used only on the index tab's border (70% mixed into --rule); the field is tinted 8%. Measured 5.80:1 light, 4.60:1 dark for the red index.

display.purpose: The name on sheet A-1. One instance on the whole site.

headline.purpose: The title of a project sheet or the resume.

title.purpose: A Schedule A project title, an MDX h2, the sign-off heading.

subtitle.purpose: An organization name in a role row; an MDX h3.

body.purpose: Project answers and MDX paragraphs, in muted ink.

body-sm.purpose: The workhorse reading size: role bullets, disclosure prose, table cells, resume points.

label.purpose: Every dt, column head, rail caption, and provenance line. Mono, uppercase, 0.14em.

data.purpose: Indices, cross-references, dates, chips, and every measured figure. Tabular, slashed-zero numerals.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system. Every transition and the draw-on animation use it.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Border and color state changes on links, actions, cross-references, and the sheet toggle.

motion.name: state-slow
motion.purpose: The figure's hover: ground fill, underline color, and the tick's press (scale 1.15, rotate -4deg).

motion.name: draw-on
motion.purpose: The site's single authored motion. The tick legend's three marks draw themselves on load, staggered 0/140/280ms, under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. Pure CSS with a fully-drawn resting state, so it cannot fail closed the way the removed IntersectionObserver implementation did.

breakpoints.name: rail-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: The project sheet's sticky margin rail becomes an auto-fit band below the prose.

breakpoints.name: columns-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Schedule A's money and ref columns narrow; the legend panel releases its width clamp.

breakpoints.name: fold
breakpoints.purpose: The mobile fold: column heads drop, work rows reflow into named grid areas, role and resume entries go single-column, the rotated stamp hides, and all horizontal padding steps down to --s-4.

components.name: Figure
components.description: The signature mechanic: a measured value carrying the pencil tick that resolves to the public source it was agreed to. A real link, so the audit trail survives keyboard use and JavaScript being off.
components.html: 22.5 pts— agreed to source: A/A noise floor, n=5 k=8
components.css: .ds-figure { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.5rem; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); padding-bottom: 1px; transition: border-color 0.2s var(--ease), background-color 0.2s var(--ease); } .ds-figure-value { font-family: var(--f-data); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1, 'zero' 1; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.375rem; } .ds-figure .ds-mark { color: var(--red); opacity: 0.55; transition: opacity 0.2s var(--ease), transform 0.2s var(--ease); } .ds-figure:hover, .ds-figure:focus-visible { border-bottom-color: var(--red); background: var(--red-wash); } .ds-figure:hover .ds-mark, .ds-figure:focus-visible .ds-mark { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.15) rotate(-4deg); } .ds-figure:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; }

components.name: Cross-reference
components.description: Blue pencil. Every link between sheets is one of these, so the index scheme (A-1, W-1..W-3, R-1) is the navigation rather than a label on top of it.
components.html: W-1opsgym
components.css: .ds-xref { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.45em; font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--blue); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid transparent; white-space: nowrap; transition: border-color 0.18s var(--ease); } .ds-xref-index { flex: none; } .ds-xref-label { color: var(--ink-muted); font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.01em; } .ds-xref-caret { flex: none; align-self: center; transition: transform 0.18s var(--ease); } .ds-xref:hover, .ds-xref:focus-visible { border-bottom-color: var(--blue); } .ds-xref:hover .ds-xref-caret { transform: translateX(2px); } .ds-xref:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Schedule
components.description: The repeating structural unit: a banded, tallied head, a ruled column-head row, green-bar banded record rows, and an accounting double rule that closes the schedule. This replaces the card grid entirely.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-schedule { background: var(--stock-raised); border-inline: 1px solid var(--rule); } .ds-schedule-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; background: var(--stock-band); border-block: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); } .ds-schedule-title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink); } .ds-label { font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-faint); } .ds-cols { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 13.5rem; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.5rem 1.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); } .ds-cols > * { font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-faint); } .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 13.5rem; gap: 1rem; padding: 1rem 1.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); color: var(--ink); } .ds-row:nth-of-type(even) { background: var(--stock-band); } .ds-money { text-align: right; } .ds-num { font-family: var(--f-data); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1, 'zero' 1; font-weight: 600; } .ds-rule-close { border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); border-bottom: 3px double var(--rule-strong); height: 4px; margin: 0; }

components.name: Index Tab
components.description: The sheet's address, printed on a folder tab seated on the rail's bottom edge so its open bottom runs into the sheet. The only place manila appears, and it appears on the border.
components.css: .ds-index-tab { position: relative; display: inline-block; font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--red); padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--manila) 8%, var(--stock-raised)); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--manila) 70%, var(--rule)); border-bottom: 0; border-radius: 3px 3px 0 0; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: A stack or coursework tag: a small square card cut from the desk stock and laid on the sheet. Always static — never interactive, selected, or a filter.
components.css: .ds-chips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; } .ds-chip { font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--ink-muted); border: 1px solid var(--rule); padding: 1px 0.5rem; background: var(--stock); } .ds-chip-tool { color: var(--ink-faint); }

components.name: Text Action
components.description: The default affordance. There is no filled button in this system: an action is mono, uppercase, and underlined in the heavy rule, going red on hover and focus. The primary variant starts red.
components.css: .ds-action { font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.8125rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); padding-bottom: 2px; transition: border-color 0.18s var(--ease), color 0.18s var(--ease); } .ds-action-primary { color: var(--red); border-bottom-color: var(--red); font-weight: 600; } .ds-action:hover, .ds-action:focus-visible { border-bottom-color: var(--red); color: var(--red); } .ds-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Download Button
components.description: The only bordered button on the site: the resume PDF on sheet R-1. Transparent field with a red border that fills with the red wash on hover.
components.html: Download PDF
components.css: .ds-download { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.8125rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--red); text-decoration: none; border: 1px solid var(--red); padding: 0.5rem 1rem; transition: background-color 0.18s var(--ease); } .ds-download:hover, .ds-download:focus-visible { background: var(--red-wash); } .ds-download:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Stamp
components.description: Applied to a document, never used as a button or a chip. Blended into the stock so the ink sits in the paper rather than on top of it.
components.html: Prepared by S. Chen Not cleared
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-block; font-family: var(--f-text); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--red); border: 2px solid var(--red); padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 2px; transform: rotate(-2.2deg); opacity: 0.82; mix-blend-mode: multiply; } .ds-stamp-blue { color: var(--blue); border-color: var(--blue); } :root[data-theme='dark'] .ds-stamp { mix-blend-mode: screen; }

components.name: Disclosure Note
components.description: Where the numbers do not fully behave. Structurally a schedule row so it reads as part of the record, and placed directly after Schedule A rather than buried in a footer.
components.html:
Disclosure — what is not done

Not cleared

Each sheet carries the limits its own repository states. They are here rather than buried because the limits are the reason to trust everything above them.
components.css: .ds-note { position: relative; padding: 1.5rem; background: var(--stock-band); border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-strong); } .ds-note-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; } .ds-mark-blue { color: var(--blue); } .ds-note-title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--f-data); font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink); } .ds-note-body { margin: 0; max-width: 70ch; font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.65; color: var(--ink-muted); } .ds-note-stamp { position: absolute; top: 2rem; right: 3rem; display: inline-block; font-family: var(--f-text); font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--blue); border: 2px solid var(--blue); padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 2px; transform: rotate(-2.2deg); opacity: 0.82; mix-blend-mode: multiply; }

narrative.overview:
This is not a portfolio of projects; it is the working papers behind them. The whole surface is built as a physical document an auditor would have on the desk: columnar analysis stock, hairline printed ruling, alternating green-bar bands, a folder tab carrying the sheet's index, and two colors of wax pencil laid over the print. The thesis the world exists to serve is that every figure carries the pencil tick that resolves to the source it was agreed to — the tick is not decoration, it is the mechanic, and it is a real link.

The world is deliberately literal about its own materials. The sheet has edges because a working paper is an object that sits on a desk rather than a page that bleeds off it. Rows are ruled and banded because that is what the stock is. Schedules are titled and tallied and closed with an accounting double rule because that convention genuinely means "this total is final." The dark theme is not an inverted palette; it is the same sheet under a desk lamp at night, keeping the green cast in the stock, the ruling, and the ink.

The category's default answer — a three-up grid of project cards — is refused outright. Structure is a schedule with named columns, and a project's headline measurement sits in the money column, right-aligned, in the data face, with its tick beside it. What makes the surface recognizable with all content removed is exactly two things: the banded schedules and the margin index.
keyCharacteristics: Bounded ruled sheet on bare stock, never a full-bleed page
Green-bar banding on alternating rows; the band is the row, never a decorative stripe
Two-color pencil vocabulary: red for agreed figures, blue for cross-references and caveats
Every measured value set in the mono data face with tabular numerals
Hairline printed ruling everywhere; no shadows, no gradients, no rounded cards
A cross-reference index (A-1, W-1–W-3, R-1) that is the navigation, not a label on it

rules.name: The Two Pencils Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two accent colors and each has one job. Red states a measured result and the actions that lead to one. Blue points somewhere — a cross-reference, a disclosure, a limit. A third accent, or red used to point and blue used to state, breaks the world's grammar.

rules.name: The Band Is The Row Rule
rules.body: Green-bar banding is applied by :nth-child(even) on real schedule rows and real table rows only. It marks the record boundary; it is never a decorative stripe, a section background chosen for variety, or a highlight for emphasis.

rules.name: The Verified Floor Rule
rules.body: --ink-faint is #575f50 light and #939e88 dark specifically because label and provenance text renders at 12–13px on the green band, and those values were picked to clear 4.5:1 against --stock-band, not against the sheet. Any new faint-ink value must be measured against the band, not the raised sheet.

rules.name: The Manila Edge Rule
rules.body: Manila carries the folder tab's edge (70% mixed into the rule), with the field tinted only 8%. A heavily tinted manila field drops the red index below the contrast floor — most sharply in the dark theme, where the mix resolves light. Measured on the shipped tab: 5.80:1 light, 4.60:1 dark. Do not push the field tint up to make the tab "read as manila."

rules.name: The Data Face Rule
rules.body: Anything a reader could copy into a spreadsheet — a figure, a date range, an index, a GPA, a phone number — is set in Sometype Mono with tabular, slashed-zero numerals. Prose is never set in the mono; the mono is never used to add texture.

rules.name: The Declared Measure Rule
rules.body: ch resolves against the element's own font-size, so a 68ch measure declared on a 1rem container yields roughly 86 characters when the text inside renders at 0.8125rem. Every prose container therefore declares the size its text is actually set at: .prose-sm sets font-size alongside its 70ch cap, and the per-surface caps (58ch, 62ch, 68ch, 70ch, 72ch) are all stated on the element that carries the type size. Never inherit a measure across a size change.

rules.name: The Balanced Head Rule
rules.body: All headings carry text-wrap: balance and letter-spacing tightening from -0.02em at title size to -0.04em at display size. Large type is always tighter, never looser.

rules.name: The Bounded Sheet Rule
rules.body: Content never touches the viewport edge. A section that wants to span the window is wrong for this world; widen the sheet or accept the edge.

rules.name: The Schedule, Not The Card Rule
rules.body: Grouped content is a schedule: a titled, tallied band of ruled rows. Cards — a floating rounded box with its own padding and border — are the category default this world exists to refuse, and are not used as page structure anywhere.

rules.name: The Wide Table Scrolls Itself Rule
rules.body: Prose in a project sheet caps at 62ch, but tables opt out because they are schedules, not prose. A table too wide for the sheet scrolls inside .table-wrap; the page body never scrolls horizontally.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no gradients, no blurs, no glows. If an element needs to separate from its surroundings, it gets a rule, a band, or a step in the stock tone — in that order of preference.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: New elements get border-radius: 0. A radius must be argued for from the physical metaphor (a stamp's bite, a folder tab's fold), never chosen for softness.

rules.name: The Drawn Mark Rule
rules.body: No glyph icons, no icon font, no arrow or check as a character. Every mark is an authored SVG path at the world's stroke weight.

dos: Do put every measurement in the data face with tabular numerals, and give it a Figure that links to the public source it was transcribed from.

Do transcribe figures exactly. 22.5 pts, −$188,718, 0.219 ft, 10.9%, 16,009 rows — nothing is rounded, embellished, or inferred, and nothing appears on the page that a linked repository, live report, or the résumé does not state.
Do carry a source in the accessible name via .sr-only, not in a title attribute.

Do keep the audit vocabulary consistent: schedule, engagements, sign-off, prepared by, not cleared, tally, index, and the closing double rule. This is a considered decision, reviewed and kept. Splitting it — engineering saying "roles" while markets says "engagements" — would break the world's single addressing language to dodge the lowest-salience text on the page. The audit-versus-accounting frame is carried by the figures, which point the right way.
Do declare a prose container's font-size on the same element as its ch measure.
Do state a new prohibition's contrast against --stock-band when the text will sit on a banded row, which most small text does.
Do address new pages with an index (A-, W-, R- families) and reach them with a CrossRef.
Do keep limits and caveats in the record. The disclosure note and the margin rail's "what is not done" are content, not disclaimers, and are never collapsed, faded, or moved to a footer.
donts: Don't use cards, a three-up project grid, or any floating rounded box as page structure.
Don't add a shadow, gradient, blur, or glow. Depth comes from three stock tones and a rule.
Don't introduce a third accent color, or use red to point and blue to state.
Don't band a section for visual variety. Banding marks a record row.
Don't use a unicode glyph or an icon font where a mark belongs; draw the path.
Don't make a mark's visibility depend on a script or an observer. Marks rest fully drawn; animation may only replay a stroke that is already there.
Don't animate anything beyond the tick legend's draw-on and the small state transitions already in the system (0.18–0.2s border, color, opacity, and the figure tick's press).
Don't tint the index tab's field to strengthen the manila; the tab's color lives on its border for a measured contrast reason.
Don't let content bleed to the viewport edge, and don't let the page scroll horizontally — a wide table scrolls inside its own wrapper.
